sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Income-Generating Real Estate Property Portfolio Trust (REIT)

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with PRC administrative overlay for WFOE establishment)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (revised, effective 1 Jan 2025); PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Registration of Market Entities (effective 1 Nov 2024); PRC Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identity Data and Transaction Records Management; Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act and Taiwan Company Act (for the Taiwan-origin parent)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarisation by a Chinese notary public, followed by either (a) an Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China when the destination state is party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, or (b) consular legalisation by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the destination state when the destination state is not an Apostille Convention party. The two paths are mutually exclusive; sequential use is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT) / China Chamber of International Commerce (CCOIC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Chinese notary public authentication followed by either Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille (Hague member destination) or Chinese Embassy/Consulate consular legalisation (non-member destination); mutually exclusive paths, never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan-origin investing shareholder or the shareholders meeting of the WFOE, as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Taiwan-origin instruments: notarisation at a Taiwan district court notary office, cross-strait verification through the Strait Exchange Foundation and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits, and then either an Apostille or consular legalisation as required by the receiving jurisdiction. For mainland China-origin instruments: Chinese notary public, then either MOFA Apostille or consular legalisation. Apostille and consular legalisation are alternative routes depending on the destination state and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered shareholders of the WFOE, filed and sealed by the Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy from SAMR plus notarisation by a Chinese notary; then either MOFA Apostille (Hague member states) or Chinese Embassy/Consulate consular legalisation (non-member states). The paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Designated corporate bank of the WFOE or the parent company's bank in Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer attestation and notarisation (for Taiwan bank letters, additionally SEF/ARATS verification if required), followed by either MOFA Apostille or consular legalisation depending on the destination state; no mixture of Apostille and consular legalisation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Beneficial Owner Registration (UBO registry excerpt)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) together with the local PBOC branch under Order No. 3
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If printed as part of the official registration record, notarise the certified hard copy, then apply either MOFA Apostille or Chinese Embassy/Consulate legalisation; if produced electronically, obtain a certified true copy with the digital verification code before notarisation. Apostille and consular legalisation are alternative and mutually exclusive paths.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, senior managers, authorised signatories and counterparties against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications lists; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) PRC Ministry of Public Security's List of Persons Subject to Anti-Terrorism and Anti-Money Laundering Measures; (v) Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission AML/CFT and sanctions lists; and (vi) adverse media and politically exposed persons (PEP) databases. Enhanced due diligence applies where any individual holds government, judicial, military or SOE positions, immediate family relations, or close associate status, or where beneficial ownership exceeds 25%. Sanctions hits require immediate internal escalation to the AML Compliance Officer, a 24-hour hold on any contemplated funding, and a SAR/STR filing if a reasonable suspicion arises. All screening must be repeatable at least twice a year and triggered by ownership changes, board changes, or negative news.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Registration System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the Enterprise Integrated Registration Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must follow the four-tier statutory structure: Administrative Division + Distinctive Name + Industry or Operating Characteristics + Organization Form. The registered name must be in simplified Chinese characters; the distinctive name element must have a coherent Mandarin pinyin transliteration and cannot be identical or similar to an existing enterprise name in the same or a related industry within the same administrative jurisdiction. English names are not filed as legal names, but where used on documentation or bank accounts must be a faithful transliteration of the Chinese name without conflicting marks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 working days after refusal, the applicant (or its entrusted agency) may submit an administrative reconsideration application to the same SAMR office that rejected the name, or directly to the higher-level Administration for Market Regulation under the PRC Administrative Reconsideration Law. The application must state the legal and factual grounds, include a copy of the rejection notice, and demonstrate that the proposed name satisfies the four-tier naming doctrine and does not fall within prohibited or sensitive tokens. If the reconsideration decision is adverse, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit in the People's Court within 15 days of receipt. To avoid time loss, the applicant should concurrently reserve up to three alternative names; a rejected name cannot be re-submitted with the same spelling or pinyin. Applicants may also seek a pre-clearance opinion from the municipal market regulator business directory before formal filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE engaged in ISIC 6499 real estate investment trust activities, a virtual office or commercial mail forwarding address is not acceptable. The PBOC, SAMR, and tax authorities require a physical business premises that corresponds to the registered address, with retained original documents (incorporation record, articles, lease of real property, shareholder registers), a dedicated company seal, and identifiable personnel. Using a registered agent-only address triggers a presumption of false registration under the PRC Company Law and can lead to cancellation, serious credit punishment, and bank account closure. A real estate trust business must demonstrate local operational substance, such as an executed commercial office lease for at least one year and the presence of at least one compliance officer, to secure banking licenses and investment permissions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) lease agreement for registered premises, (2) company letterhead and seal at the registered address, (3) presence of statutory representatives and financial/AML personnel during business hours, (4) production of UBO register and board minutes, (5) evidence of actual REIT-related activities (trust indentures, portfolio lease contracts, dividend policy). Quantified risk: high (60-70%) for newly established WFOEs in regulated trust/asset management because municipal tax bureaus and SAMR conduct random on-site verification within the first 12 months; the risk rises to 85% if the registered address is in a residential building, a shared service centre, or a class-B building with fewer than 10 employees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and incorporation filing fee (government registry fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), local municipal branch
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee is charged under the current PRC registry fee schedule; the amount is nil.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal engraving set (company, finance, legal representative, contract, duplicate five seals)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed commercial seal engraving service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate in Tier-1 Chinese cities; not a government fixed tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarisation of corporate documents (certificate of incorporation, AoA, board resolution, UBO register excerpt)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Provincial pricing authority schedule for notarisation fees, charged per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille fee by Ministry of Foreign Affairs (per document bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China (Consular Department)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official MOFA scale per Apostille certificate; if destination is a non-Hague state, this line is not used.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalisation fee by Chinese Embassy or Consulate (only if destination state is not an Apostille Convention party)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese Embassy or Consulate in the destination jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule for non-Hague destinations; mutually exclusive with Apostille.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cross-strait verification fee for Taiwan-origin notarised documents (SEF and ARATS processing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Strait Exchange Foundation (Taiwan) and Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (mainland)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Published processing fee charged per notarised instrument; applicable only to Taiwan-origin documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English translation of Chinese and Taiwan corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Accredited translation agency or sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate per 1,000 characters with certification statement and translator's seal.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and UBO piercing opinion (outside counsel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed PRC law firm or foreign counsel authorised to advise on cross-border structure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed fee under engagement letter or hourly benchmark of USD 300 to USD 800 per attorney hour.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter fee and corporate bank officer attestation/notarisation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published tariff for corporate reference letters plus notarial/attestation fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial physical registered office lease deposit and first-year pro-rata rent (for REIT operational substance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Landlord / lessor of commercial premises under registered office lease
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market lease rate for Grade A or Grade B office space; no government fixed tariff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, Articles 1, 2, 8, 18, 100, 128, 129, 161, 172, 200, 387 and 403; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 4, 7 and 8; Real Estate Securitization Act, Article 10 (for REIT licensing); if the foreign shareholder is a mainland China entity, the Mainland Investment Permission Regulations also apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (MOEA DOC); foreign investment entry window: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign Investment Approval Application (Investment Commission, MOEA) and Limited Liability Company Incorporation Registration Application (MOEA DOC One-Stop Company Establishment Filing)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Taiwan Company Act for a limited liability WFOE; there is no blocked escrow capital rule and the incorporators may fix paid-in capital at a commercially sufficient amount. However, because the proposed scope is a Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT), the Financial Supervisory Commission requires the licensed trustee/operator to maintain adequate net worth and capital as a post-incorporation licensing condition, which is a supervisory solvency requirement and not a formation escrow rule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [●] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (TAIWAN). The undersigned incorporator and sole shareholder, acting in writing and without a general meeting in accordance with the Taiwan Company Act and the Articles of Incorporation, hereby adopts the following first board resolutions, effective upon the date of the issuance of the Company's establishment registration certificate by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND PAID-IN CAPITAL. The subscription to the Company's registered share capital of New Taiwan Dollars [●], consisting of [●] fully paid ordinary shares with a par value of New Taiwan Dollars [●] each, is hereby ratified, confirmed, and accepted. The Board acknowledges receipt of the full amount of the paid-in capital in the Company's designated bank deposit account, and confirms that no share has been issued for consideration other than cash unless the consideration has been lawfully verified by a certified public accountant. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Company shall open and maintain corporate accounts at [●] Bank, Taiwan Branch. The Chairman, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer, acting in any two-person combination, are hereby authorized to execute account opening documentation, wire instructions, foreign exchange transactions, deposit agreements, and all related certificates. Banking instruments above New Taiwan Dollars [●] must bear two authorized signatures. This authority continues until revoked by a later board resolution. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company shall be located at [●], Taiwan. The Board adopts this office as the statutory seat of the Company, the address for service of judicial and administrative process, and the primary place where the corporate books and records will be maintained. Management is authorized to execute the lease, pay deposit and rent, and file the address with the competent authority. Any relocation requires a subsequent board resolution and re-registration. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS. The following persons are appointed to the offices indicated: [●] as Director and General Manager; [●] as Supervisor, if required; [●] as Company Secretary; and [●] as Anti-Money-Laundering Compliance Officer and principal officer for Financial Supervisory Commission communications. Each appointee declares acceptance, and the Company shall file their particulars with the registry and taxation authorities immediately upon incorporation. 5. GOVERNANCE AND LICENSING. The Board delegates to the General Manager the authority to prepare and submit all regulatory applications, including the real estate investment trust authorization to the Financial Supervisory Commission, to open payroll facilities, and to manage ordinary-course contracts. The Board ratifies all authorized expenses incurred in connection with this resolution and directs the officers to complete all statutory filings, publication requirements, and tax registrations. This resolution may not be amended unless by a duly convened subsequent board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Step 1 - Foreign Investment Approval and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC); One-Stop Company Registration Portal (https://onestop.nat.gov.tw)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Foreign Investment Approval Application online through MOEAIC or the One-Stop Portal. The application must include Chinese and English company name choices, the precise ISIC 6499 scope, and the proposed registered capital. The foreign corporate shareholder must provide a notarized certificate of incorporation, a board resolution authorizing the creation of the Taiwan WFOE, and a power of attorney for the in-country representative. MOEAIC reviews national security, foreign exchange, and any land-relevant limitations. Approval must be obtained before the capital remittance or incorporation filing. Retain the approval number because it must be cited in the bank remittance instructions and registration application.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval application form
Notarized certificate of incorporation and board resolution of the foreign parent
Power of attorney appointing the Taiwan representative
Business plan and REIT scope narrative
Passport or corporate identity documents of directors and shareholders
Proposed articles of incorporation and name reservation receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEAIC issues a clarification request, submit the missing documents or revised business scope within 30 days. If approval is denied, file an administrative appeal with the Executive Yuan within 30 days under the Administrative Appeal Act, or modify the business scope and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Step 2 - Capital Remittance, Bank Account Opening, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Taiwan licensed commercial bank and a Taiwan-certified public accountant (CPA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After MOEAIC approval, open a temporary capital deposit account at a Taiwan licensed bank. Remit the approved foreign exchange amount into this account and convert into New Taiwan Dollars. Obtain the bank's foreign exchange settlement certificate and inward remittance notice. Engage a certified public accountant to verify actual receipt of paid-in capital and issue a CPA capital verification report confirming that the shareholders' ledger and bank statements are consistent with the articles of incorporation. The report should be dated shortly before the company registration filing. For a REIT-scope WFOE, the initial capital may later be increased to meet FSC financial soundness requirements, but the formation itself follows ordinary WFOE capital verification procedures.
required_dossiers: MOEAIC Foreign Investment Approval letter
Bank inward remittance and foreign exchange settlement certificates
Temporary bank account statement showing credited capital
Draft articles of incorporation showing share capital
Identity documents for shareholders and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank identifies a foreign exchange or remittance purpose issue, correct the remittance code and resubmit. If the CPA refuses to issue a clean capital verification, cure the subscription discrepancy or re-remit funds before proceeding to incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Step 3 - Company Incorporation Filing with MOEA Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (MOEA DOC) via the Company and Commerce One-Stop Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application electronically with MOEA DOC using the MOEAIC approval number and the CPA capital verification report. Submit the articles of incorporation, the first board resolution adopting the registered office and statutory officers, the lease or occupancy certificate for the registered address, and payment of the filing fee. The registrar will examine the legality of the company name, scope, capital schedule, director qualifications, and compliance with Taiwan Company Act requirements. Upon approval, MOEA DOC issues the company establishment registration certificate and assigns the unified tax number. The WFOE legally exists at this point; no REIT issuance or regulated trust activity may commence before the later FSC license.
required_dossiers: Company incorporation application form
Articles of incorporation
First board resolution
CPA capital verification report
Foreign Investment Approval letter
Office lease agreement or consent letter for registered office
Identification and residence certificates of officers
Filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA DOC issues a correction notice, deliver the corrected filings within the stated period, usually 15 days. If the application is rejected, request written reasons and file an administrative appeal within 30 days, or withdraw and refile after curing the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Step 4 - Tax, Labor, and Municipal Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau (local branch); municipal labor affairs and health insurance authorities; local government commerce bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete tax registration to formalize the unified business tax number, and register for the Uniform Invoice scheme if the company will issue invoices. Register as a withholding taxpayer for employee income tax, labor insurance, health insurance, and labor pension contributions. File any required municipal business registration with the local commerce bureau and verify that the office premises comply with zoning and building use regulations. Because the WFOE is a financial-sector REIT candidate, designate the AML compliance officer and establish the initial AML/CFT framework required by the Money Laundering Control Act. This step ensures operating legality before hiring employees or executing third-party contracts.
required_dossiers: Company establishment registration certificate
Unified tax number certificate
Company seal and seal authorization card
Lease agreement and building compliance certificate
Director and shareholder identification
Employee payroll and insurance registration forms
AML compliance policy and officer designation statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or labor authority flags inconsistencies, submit corrections within the statutory response period and pay any late fees. If municipal zoning clearance fails, relocate the registered office and re-file the address change with MOEA DOC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Step 5 - Financial Supervisory Commission REIT Licensing and Business Commencement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), Securities and Futures Bureau; Taiwan Stock Exchange or Taipei Exchange if a public offering is contemplated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, submit the REIT business plan to the FSC under Article 10 of the Real Estate Securitization Act. The application must include the real estate trust deed, the proposed portfolio of income-generating real property, a valuation report by a licensed property appraiser, internal control and conflict-of-interest policies, an AML/CFT program, and audited capital or solvency evidence. The FSC will conduct a substantive review of management fitness, investor protection, and corporate governance. Approval must be obtained before soliciting investors or distributing REIT securities. If the foreign parent is subject to additional cross-border governance conditions, the WFOE must implement them before commencing regulated operations. Operating without the FSC license is prohibited and may result in penalties under the Real Estate Securitization Act.
required_dossiers: FSC application for REIT/trustee institution approval
Real estate trust deed and REIT issuance plan
Property appraisal and due diligence reports
First board resolution approving the FSC filing
Corporate bylaws and conflict-of-interest policies
AML/CFT policy and officer appointment
Financial statements and capital compliance report
Foreign investor approval and shareholding structure disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC queries the application, respond within 30 days with supplemental materials. If the FSC denies the application, review the denial basis, amend the proposal, and resubmit, or file an administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan within 30 days. During review, the company may only perform preparatory activities and may not solicit investors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission, Securities and Futures Bureau; municipal Department of Economic Development for administrative use exemptions and local zoning clearance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) Trustee/Operator License under the Real Estate Securitization Act (Taiwan) - FSC License for the Issuance and Operation of Real Estate Investment Trust Beneficiary Securities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Pure Financial Trust Activity (ISIC 6499). The WFOE does not conduct physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing, so no Environmental Impact Assessment is required for the corporate entity. If the WFOE later acquires or develops underlying real property, the specific project must be screened by the competent municipal EIA committee before construction.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the WFOE head office because it generates no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste. Any underlying real estate development or renovation would be subject to Taiwan EPA numeric standards at the asset level, including effluent standards under the Water Pollution Control Act, VOC controls under the Air Pollution Control Act, and hazardous waste manifesting under the Waste Disposal Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The WFOE administrative office must obtain a fire safety inspection certificate under Article 6 of the Fire Services Act from the local county/city fire department and must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act. Underlying REIT buildings must maintain their own lawful building-use permits, fire safety equipment, public safety insurance, and structural compliance certificates in the name of the trust or asset-holding entity; civil defense shelter exemptions apply to the financial standby office.

stage_2.governance_notes: No physical manufacturing or chemical license is required. The material regulatory approval is the Financial Supervisory Commission REIT license, which is mandatory before any regulated real estate trust activity may commence. The entity must also maintain a current registered office, statutory officers, and AML/CFT compliance framework throughout the life of the Taiwan WFOE.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online corporate portal is the STA Electronic Tax Service Platform (e-Tax), used for corporate income tax, VAT, and non-resident withholding filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. The WFOE obtains its business licence from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); the system generates the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which functions as the taxpayer identification number. 2. SAMR sends the registration record to the STA, and the WFOE completes tax registration at the competent local STA office within 30 days. 3. The WFOE opens the enterprise tax file and elects VAT status: general taxpayer if annual taxable sales already exceed or are expected to exceed RMB 5,000,000, otherwise small-scale taxpayer. 4. A foreign non-resident enterprise, such as the Taiwan parent, with China-sourced income must separately register as a non-resident taxpayer with the STA, appoint a local withholding agent, and submit its tax residence certificate and evidence of the withholding arrangement through the e-Tax portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under PRC Corporate Income Tax Law; China does not permit check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity elections for a WFOE limited liability company. Only the VAT general/small-scale taxpayer election is available, and it is a VAT collection election rather than an income tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under PRC VAT law, administered by the STA
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 (annual taxable sales floor triggering mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; all newly formed WFOEs must register for tax regardless of turnover)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory use of the STA-authorized electronic invoice platform. VAT invoices must contain a digital signature, unique invoice number and QR code, and invoice data is reported to the STA in near real time. Red-blue invoice reconciliation and automatic clearance controls are required before any refund or credit is granted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT export treatment applies to goods physically exported from China that receive customs release, and to designated cross-border services consumed wholly outside China, including certain technology, R&D, and business process services. For a REIT, domestic real estate rental and disposal income is not zero-rated; only cross-border supplies satisfying the 'fully consumed outside China' test qualify.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration (export Bill of Entry equivalent) with electronic customs release confirmation
Bill of Lading / sea waybill / airway bill evidencing cross-border carriage
Commercial invoice showing export price and delivery terms
Bank export proceeds settlement record / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent SAFE foreign exchange collection receipt
Export VAT special invoice or procurement invoice for input VAT refund support
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unverified or fraudulent export zero-rating claims are retrospectively clawed back by the STA, with daily late-payment interest and penalties under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law, generally 50% to 500% of the evaded tax; deliberate false export VAT refund claims also expose senior officers to criminal liability under PRC criminal law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with substantial administrative control over the capital account. The WFOE's current account, comprising service fees, dividends from operations, trade payments, and operating expenses, is generally convertible on a bona fide basis, but every payment must pass through a designated foreign exchange bank that verifies documentation and files transaction codes with the SAFE monitoring system. The capital account—equity injection, shareholder loans, outward transfers, offshore investment, and liquidation proceeds—is not freely convertible and requires either SAFE registration, prior approval, or a specific quota. Profit remittance to a Taiwan shareholder is permitted only after the annual statutory audit is completed, the foreign investor's share of distributable profits is determined using Chinese GAAP, and deemed tax obligations are settled; the bank will require the SAFE FDI registration certificate, audited financial statements, and the board's profit distribution resolution. Export surrender obligations are currently non-mandatory in percentage terms but receipts must be repatriated within 180 days after the export declaration date, and enterprises may either keep foreign exchange or voluntarily sell to banks. Cross-strait remittances receive enhanced regulatory review because of the political sensitivity, and banks must ensure that the intended economic purpose matches the reported purpose code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign exchange receipts must be repatriated to China through bank channels within 180 days from the date of export customs declaration. There is no statutory mandatory conversion percentage; the WFOE may either retain the proceeds in its foreign currency current account or voluntarily sell them to a designated bank. Repatriation must be reported under the Trade Monitoring System with matching electronic customs data, invoices, and logistics records.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational RMB/FCY Account / FDI Capital Verification Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs and non-bank payment institutions are legally barred from providing onshore RMB settlement accounts, foreign exchange capital accounts, SAFE registration services, or profit remittance processing for a mainland China WFOE. Such EMIs may support ancillary cross-border e-commerce collection in certain open pilot zones, but they cannot act as the primary treasury bank for FDI injections, capital verification, tax clearance, or dividend repatriation under China's capital account controls. All treasury-grade foreign exchange flows must be executed through a licensed designated onshore bank connected to SAFE's monitoring systems.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for the statutory legal representative and the financial officer at the chosen bank outlet for the initial account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not routinely available for an onshore WFOE; non-resident Taiwan directors or shareholders must sign powers of attorney that are notarized in Taiwan and authenticated by a designated cross-strait service institution, and original passports, Taiwan resident certificates, and company seals must be presented at the bank. Some banks may accept a remote video interview after relationship manager introduction, but a physical signatory visit is still the default for foreign-owned entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank's AML screening detects a Taiwan shareholder whose name appears on a negative news or watchlist by false-positive match, making the account onboarding subject to enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide passport or Taiwan resident certificate, proof of name change if applicable, a notarized aliases declaration, a negative news explanation with evidence, and a certified police clearance or attestation from Taiwan's Investment Commission confirming no legal enforcement actions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The initial capital contribution is routed from a third-party Hong Kong shell account rather than directly from the Taiwan parent account, triggering source-of-funds and anti-avoidance scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply an intercompany financing deed, the Taiwan parent's board resolution authorizing the third-party payment, a complete bank statement trail from Taiwan to Hong Kong to the WFOE, and a tax opinion or tax equalization letter explaining the routing rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE's declared REIT business scope has no corresponding asset-management license; the bank's compliance department questions whether the entity is being created for real estate capital flight rather than genuine operation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the statutory REIT permission or licensure from the relevant mainland regulator, the trust deed or fund prospectus, a term sheet for the first property acquisition, and audited financial projections showing rental income and distribution capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank flags the cross-border dividend remittance to Taiwan as high risk due to missing deemed tax declarations, uncertain cross-strait tax treatment, or failure to complete the annual renewal of the SAFE FDI file.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble a complete tax settlement certificate, the annual audit report, the foreign investor's profit distribution resolution, the updated SAFE FDI registration record, and the Taiwan shareholder's tax attestation of corporate residency to allow treaty or cross-strait tax treatment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must wire the equity capital through a SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's foreign currency capital account at a designated onshore bank, using the SAFE FDI registration code and the purpose code reflecting foreign direct investment capital injection. The bank will execute real-name verification, check the negative list for restricted industries, and perform foreign exchange settlement strictly in accordance with the registered capital item. After the funds arrive, the WFOE obtains a capital verification report from a licensed CPA firm and files the FDI registry update. The remittance reference must cite the SAFE FDI certificate number and the legal name of the WFOE to avoid quarantine or rejection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outgoing payments, including profit dividend distributions to the Taiwan shareholder, must be routed through the onshore bank via SWIFT MT103 using the profit remittance purpose code after completion of the annual statutory audit and tax settlement. For operational cross-border trade settlements, use documentary collections or commercial letters of credit when counterparty risk requires collateralization; for simple trade or open account transactions, use MT103 with attached invoice, transport documents, and customs records. Every outbound payment must pass the bank's collection, SAFE monitoring, and Taiwan cross-strait compliance screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD forward contracts with real underlying FX exposure
FX swaps combining spot and forward legs for temporary liquidity management
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for hedged medium-term USD or CNY debt structures
Onshore CNY options and structured collars on a real-need basis; participation in offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) is prohibited for the onshore WFOE

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting (AGM) for adoption of audited financial statements, business report and profit-distribution resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; the adopted resolution is thereafter filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year - for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June of the next year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM by the statutory deadline permits any shareholder to request MOEA to convene a meeting; directors may be fined TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000; continued default can lead to administrative dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Post-AGM filing of the approved annual financial statements, business report and profit-distribution proposal with the Company Registration Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Department of Commercial Services (Company Registration Information System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the AGM (which itself must be held by 30 June); therefore effectively by 15 July for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or failure to file triggers a warning and administrative fine of TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000; continuing non-filing is regarded as a serious registration irregularity and may lead to administrative strike-off/dissolution by MOEA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return and payment (including undistributed surplus tax regulation items)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, competent to the registered address of the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the following year for a 31 December fiscal year; for special fiscal years, within three months of the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Where the return is not filed voluntarily, the tax authority issues a notice after which a 15% late-filing surcharge is imposed on the assessed tax, plus a 1% monthly delinquency surcharge for up to 30 days and statutory interest on unpaid tax; persistent non-compliance may lead to property seizure, compulsory execution and travel restraint.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and registration of major shareholders and ultimate beneficial ownership (Company Act Article 22-1 register update)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Company Registration Information System; company registers maintained at the registered office for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after any change in directors, supervisors, managers or shareholders holding more than 10%; when no change occurs, legal confirmation in the annual post-AGM filing no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with Article 22-1 is punishable by a fine of TWD 50,000 to TWD 250,000 per violation for the responsible representatives; repeated or material violations support strike-off by MOEA and criminal liability under the Money Laundering Control Act in a designated non-financial business context.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit is required where (i) paid-in capital is TWD 30,000,000 or more, (ii) net operating revenue in the fiscal year is TWD 100,000,000 or more, (iii) the enterprise has 200 or more regular employees at the balance-sheet date, or (iv) the entity is an issuer, a real estate investment trust (REIT) or a securitization institution subject to the Real Estate Securitization Act and Financial Supervisory Commission supervision. These thresholds follow Taiwan Company Act Article 20 and the related enforcement rules. For this REIT-activity WFOE, the CPA audit mandate therefore applies irrespective of the size tests.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in New Taiwan Dollars under the generally accepted accounting principles applicable in Taiwan. Public companies and REITs must apply Taiwan IFRS (TW IFRS) as endorsed and issued by the Financial Supervisory Commission; non-public SMEs may apply the Taiwan SME Financial Reporting Standards (SME-IFRS/ROC GAAP) where elected, but the REIT scope in this payload triggers full TW IFRS reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the company must register and file with MOEA the names of shareholders holding more than 10%, directors, supervisors and managers. The register of members must be updated within 30 days of any transfer; the MOEA Article 22-1 filing must be made within 15 days of any change. As part of the annual maintenance cycle, the company must reconfirm the beneficial ownership information in the post-AGM filing by 30 June; in addition, in its capacity as a real estate investment trust, it must maintain and, upon FSC request, present a full UBO manual covering natural-person beneficial owners with 25% or greater interest for AML due-diligence purposes.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 3,000 per year for registered office, company secretary and professional agent services in Taiwan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 30,000 per year depending on asset size, transaction volume and audit risk associated with a REIT-licensed WFOE

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket tax holiday for ordinary WFOEs; qualifying encouraged-industry enterprises in Western Regions or select Free Trade Zones may apply 15%; small low-profit enterprises are taxed at 20% with a reduced taxable-income band; an additional 100% super-deduction is available for qualifying R&D expenses; publicly listed REITs under the PRC public REITs pilot may receive special tax deferral treatment, but a wholly foreign-owned private REIT trust generally remains subject to standard 25% entity-level CIT; no patent box applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: A100000 PRC Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (A-class) filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal, together with Schedule A105000 Special Tax Adjustment Items and the annual related-party transaction disclosure schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayments must be filed and paid within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the annual final return and settlement must be filed within 5 months of fiscal year-end, i.e. on or before 31 May for a calendar-year enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross rental income, service charges, property management fees, and other operating receipts attributable to the real estate investment trust portfolio, inclusive of any non-VAT revenue items but exclusive of output VAT collected from tenants.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: As a PRC-incorporated WFOE, the entity is a PRC tax resident and must declare worldwide income; for Taiwan-source rental income derived through overseas real estate, claim foreign tax credits. All PRC-source leasing income must be shown before any distribution to the Taiwan investor; rental revenue should be reconciled with VAT returns, property tax filings, and lease registers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 2 - Cost of Main Operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of maintaining and operating the trust property, including depreciation on investment properties, utilities, repairs, maintenance, insurance, and directly attributable property staff wages.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capitalize all acquisition, construction, and major refurbishment costs; no deduction is allowed for the Taiwan shareholder's investment capital or trust unit payments. Related-party maintenance and construction services must be arm's length and supported by contemporaneous documentation to avoid a downward adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, property tax, urban land use tax, stamp duty, and any land appreciation tax payable on disposal of real property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only PRC taxes borne by the WFOE. The 10% dividend withholding tax, Taiwan corporate income tax, or any PRC withholding tax on distribution to a Taiwanese shareholder is a non-deductible income tax item and cannot be claimed in this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Line 4 - Selling Expenses and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Leasing commissions, marketing costs, legal and accounting fees, professional manager fees, office expenses, and general overhead of the trust operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entertainment expense deductions are limited to 60% of the expense and 5% of gross revenue; advertising deductions are limited to 15% of revenue. Payments to the Taiwan parent or related party for management, consulting, and technical services must satisfy actual substance, benefit, and arm's length tests, otherwise the Special Tax Adjustment mechanism will add the amount back to taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense on property acquisition loans, refinancing, bank charges, and realized foreign-exchange losses on intercompany borrowings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to the Taiwan shareholder or affiliate is deductible only to the extent of the 2:1 debt-to-equity thin-capitalization safe harbour and only at an arm's length rate. The WFOE must withhold 10% EIT on interest remitted to the Taiwan lender unless a tax treaty reduction, or the not-yet-effective Cross-Strait tax agreement, applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 6 - Investment Income, Fair Value Gains and Asset Disposal Gains
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends from project subsidiaries, interest income, fair-value movements on investment properties if adopted under accounting standards, and gains or losses on disposal of real estate or equity in special purpose vehicles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accounting fair-value gains must be reconciled to historical cost tax basis unless a deemed sale triggers recognition; capital gains from PRC real estate and from sale of shares in PRC operating companies are taxable at the normal 25% rate, and no participation exemption is available for WFOE shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Grants, insurance compensation, penalties received, waiver-of-debt gains, and other income outside ordinary trust operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Debt forgiveness by the Taiwan parent is taxable income to the WFOE; gratuitous transfer of assets from a non-resident shareholder is taxable at fair market value under the substance-over-form rules. Such items should not be netted against distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit computed as operating profit plus non-operating income less non-operating expenses, before tax adjustments and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This accounting-profit figure is the starting point of the annual reconciliation; it must match the standalone financial statements of the WFOE and should not include the Taiwan investor's equity earnings unless the WFOE bears the investment in an underlying operating PRC subsidiary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 9 - Tax Adjustment Increase and Decrease
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences, including non-deductible related-party management fees, excess advertising and entertainment expenses, depreciation differences, revenue timing, and transfer-pricing or GAAR recharacterizations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must attach Schedule A105000 and, where applicable, a local file reflecting all Taiwan-related transactions. Failure to document cross-border payments or to file the related-party transaction schedule in a timely manner exposes the taxpayer to special tax adjustment and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after tax-adjusting items but before applying the deductible loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss carryforward is limited to five years; REIT operating losses cannot be distributed or allocated to Taiwanese beneficiaries. A loss-generating WFOE with continuous Taiwan management-fee payments is a red flag for transfer pricing audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 11 - Tentative Tax at Headline Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income computed at the 25% corporate income tax rate, or the lower 15% encouraged industry rate or 20% small low-profit rate if the entity qualifies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a preferential rate is claimed, maintain the qualification certificate, business operation records, and employee and staffing evidence showing core income-generating activities in the PRC; a WFOE that is a mere holding shell cannot benefit from the reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 12 - Tax Credits and Prepaid Taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for quarterly CIT instalments already prepaid, plus foreign tax credit for PRC taxes payable on income sourced through overseas leasing structures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE may credit Taiwan corporate income tax attributable to Taiwan-source income for which a Taiwan payment receipt is obtained, limited to the PRC tax payable on that foreign income; no credit is available for the 10% withholding tax imposed on the Taiwan shareholder's dividend distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers TCAL Art. 62 penalties of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the outstanding tax under Art. 32; underpayment due to fraudulent evasion is sanctioned at 50% to 500% of the evaded tax under Art. 63; criminal prosecution under PRC Criminal Law Art. 201 can arise where the tax evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and represents more than 10% of the taxable amount, with imprisonment of up to three years for relatively large amounts and three to seven years for huge amounts, together with fines and confiscation.
